headline: US Shale Giants Curb Drilling Spend Despite Higher Crude Prices
summary: Major US shale producers are maintaining conservative spending on drilling this year despite an average $20 per barrel increase in WTI crude. Smaller independents have begun expanding drilling activity.
why: Capital discipline by dominant US shale operators restrains supply growth and supports shareholder returns across the energy sector.

impacts.name: WTI Crude
impacts.why: Restrained drilling by large shale operators limits US crude production growth.
